newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares drift down, seen up in coming weeks.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares drift down, seen up in coming weeks.

text.p: Leading Russian shares eased on thin volumes on Tuesday, and some traders said the market could head lower if reluctant investors continued to hold back.
But they said the upward trend would resume in the next few weeks.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index closed at 359.37 on a total market turnover of $43.7 million. The index closed at a record high of 366.22 on Monday.
"Investors are passive for now on blue chips," said one trader at a Western investment company. "If the passivity continues, the market will be lower."
National electricity company UES edged up to $0.3175 from Monday's closing $0.3172 while regional power utility Mosenergo slipped to $1.322 from $1.329.
Natural gas producer Gazprom fell to $0.600 from $0.620 previously.

Other traders said the market had already discounted a rise in U.S. interest rates, which some economists say could result from Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Reserve, and would head up again after a short breather.
"If they raise rates we will not see a big reaction since people have been expecting it a long time," said ING Barings chief equities trader Peter Kizenko.
"The trend remains up, but I think the market will be fairly quiet until next week."
But the trader at the Western firm said the market could remain sluggish for some time yet.

"The market was correcting yesterday afternoon and this morning but there will be another rise -- the upward movement will resume within about two weeks to a month: clients are still inclined to buy."
